one_month_reasoning: The window (to 2026-11-01) most likely contains no earnings: fiscal Q3 ends around Oct 3, and Lattice reported Q2 on Aug 4, about 4.5 weeks after the July 4 quarter-end. On that cadence Q3 results should land around Nov 3, just after the window. The date had not been announced when I checked, so there is some chance it falls inside. The only dated filing-based event is the first lock-up release on the AMI consideration shares: per the 7/27/2026 8-K, 25% of the ~5.2M shares are freed after each 90 days, so about 1.3M shares (~0.9% of the 142.0M outstanding) free up around Oct 25. THL also holds two underwritten block-trade rights, so a block sale is a modest overhang. The stock rallied from $111 (week of 9/14) to $134 (+21% in two weeks), which adds a little short-term reversal risk. Against that, Q3 guidance ($245-265M revenue, $0.54-0.58 EPS) is well above the Street's earlier numbers, and pre-earnings run-ups into a beat-and-raise pattern are common. These roughly cancel, so I keep a near-symmetric lognormal centred at about $134 with monthly vol of 61%/3.5 = 17.4%, slightly shaded down for the block-trade overhang.

fair_value.method: Blend of a forward P/E (NTM EPS of about $3.80 as of Oct 2027 x 38 = $144) and EV/NTM sales (about $1.6B x 12, less about $0.45B net debt, over 144M shares = $130). Weights are 60/40, giving about $138.

methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Oct 2027 (Q4'27-Q3'28) of about $3.80 x 38 = $144. 2027E non-GAAP EPS of about $3.20 on about $1.38B revenue.

inputs_detail.derivation: FPGA starts from the Q3'26 guide of $220M and grows about 7% q/q, giving about $1.12B for 2027. Management says 2027 is 'pretty much booked'. AMI: more than $200M in CY2026 x 1.25 (management's 2027 growth comment) gives about $260M.
CFO's '70-ish%' long-term GM. Opex runs from the Q3 guide of $83-90M per quarter and grows about 10%.

inputs_detail.value: about $40M interest on the $925M term loan (deleveraging); 6-8% tax
inputs_detail.derivation: Term SOFR plus 1.00-1.75% on a balance that declines as FCF repays it. Q3 tax guide is 4-6%, rising modestly.
142.03M outstanding at 7/30/2026 (includes about 5.2M AMI shares), plus about 2M dilution from RSUs and AMI employee grants.
2027E EPS of $3.20 grown about 20%, consistent with the $3B-by-2030 revenue target (about 30% CAGR) and EPS growing faster than revenue.

The stock trades at about 45x my NTM EPS today (about $3.00) and about 42x 2027E. I assume modest compression as growth slows from 60%+ toward 25-30% and the company carries leverage. Consensus 2027 EPS of $2.41 (likely pre-AMI/stale) implies Street targets of $148-165, which would be 60x+ on that base.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Oct 2027 of about $1.6B x 12 = EV $19.2B, less net debt of about $0.45B, over 144M shares = $130.

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027E of $1.38B rolled forward at about 20% growth, on the $3B-by-2030 trajectory.

Current EV is about $19.9B (134 x 142M + about $0.83B net debt), or about 15x my NTM revenue of $1.3B. I compress to 12x for slowing growth and the lower-multiple firmware mix, while keeping a premium for a 40%+ EBITDA margin.

$925M term loan drawn 7/27/2026 against about $173M cash at 7/4/2026 less the cash part of the purchase gives net debt of about $0.83B at close. FCF of about $450M/yr (Q2 FCF margin 40%) is partly applied to the target of under 2x leverage by end-2027.

bear.story: AI server capex digests in 2027, or distributor inventory corrects (distributors are now 95% of revenue, up from 84%). FPGA growth stalls, 2027 EPS comes in around $2.6, and the multiple compresses to about 28x. Leverage of about $0.8B amplifies the de-rating.

base.story: The $1.2B exit run rate holds, 2027 revenue is about $1.38B, EPS is about $3.2 and NTM EPS about $3.8 at the horizon, valued at about 38x. Deleveraging is on track.

bull.story: FPGA attach per AI server keeps rising (more than 3 units per server, ASP above $4), AMI grows 25%+, and the $3B-2030 path gains credibility. NTM EPS of about $4.6 x 45x.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $85 (about 27x my 2027E EPS, and under the August-September lows of $104-110 by a wide margin), the market would be pricing an end to the AI-server FPGA growth leg. Likely causes are a guide-down showing the 'pretty much booked' 2027 visibility was distributor stocking, or an AMI customer-neutrality loss with hyperscalers. Ordinary semiconductor volatility at 61% annual vol would not usually take it there without such news.

key_uncertainties: Durability of AI-server-driven Compute & Communications growth (+83% y/y in Q2), and whether distributor sell-in (95% of revenue) is running ahead of sell-through
AMI integration and silicon-neutrality: hyperscaler and OEM customers might move firmware work away from a chip vendor
Multiple: the stock sits at about 45x NTM EPS, so a small slowdown can cause outsized de-rating
Assembly capacity constraints and cost pass-through flagged on the Q2 call
Leverage of about $0.8B of net debt after the AMI close, plus share overhang from THL lock-up releases and block-trade rights
reasoning: Primary documents show a sharp inflection. Q2'26 revenue was $201.1M (+62% y/y), non-GAAP EPS $0.53 (beating the top of guidance), adjusted EBITDA margin 43% and FCF margin 40%. Compute & Communications was $125.9M (62.6% of revenue). Q3 guidance is $210-230M for FPGA (+65% y/y) and $245-265M including about two months of AMI, with EPS of $0.54-0.58. The AMI deal ($1.65B: about $1B cash and 5.2M shares) closed 7/27, funded with a $925M term loan. Shares outstanding were 142.0M on 7/30. On the call, management guided to a $1.2B exit-2026 run rate, said 2027 is 'pretty much booked', expects AMI to grow 25% in 2027, targets under 2x leverage by end-2027, and set a $3B-by-2030 goal. My bottom-up 2027E is about $1.38B revenue and about $3.20 EPS, well above the stale web consensus of $2.41. Applying a compressed but premium multiple gives a fair value of about $138, close to the $134 price. The stock is fully valued rather than cheap, so I centre the distribution near spot (median about $136). Dispersion: realized vol is 61%, and the stock swung between $104 and $157 in the last four months alone. I use an effective 12-month log-vol of about 0.55, slightly below realized because the business visibility is better than in past cycles, and the bear/bull scenarios (25/50/25 at $75/$145/$215) cross-check the tails. Filing-only details the recaps skip: distributor concentration rose to 95% of revenue (two distributors hold 49% and 39% of AR), a $24M step-up in cash paid for software/IP licenses, $32.9M of RSU tax withholding in 1H, the AMI lock-up schedule, and routine 10b5-1 insider sales in Aug-Sep (about $0.6M). Limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were unavailable because of plan and rate limits. I could not fetch the IR-hosted transcript (503) and used a transcript summary page instead. Consensus figures come from an aggregator and may be stale.
